title: Comparative Extraction of Polyphenolic Co-pigments and Proteins from Residual Annatto (Bixa orellana L.) seeds
content: Annatto (Bixa orellana L.) seed residues retain valuable bioactive compounds such as bixin, phenolic compounds and proteins, supporting their potential for reuse. This study evaluated three green extraction methods—maceration (ME), ultrasound-assisted ex-traction (UAE), and subcritical water extraction (SWE)—to recover these compounds. ME and UAE were conducted at 70 °C using different solid-to-solvent ratios (1:10 and 1:30 g/mL) and various solvents (water, ethanol, water/ethanol, methanol, and wa-ter/methanol mixtures). SWE was carried out at 40 bar and 1:30 g/mL, with temperatures of 100, 120 and 140 ºC. Extraction efficiency was assessed based on yield, bixin and protein contents, antioxidant activity (via DPPH, FRAP, ABTS assays), and total phenolic content (TPC). Across all extractions, a 1:30 g/mL ratio provided superior extraction results. SWE at 140 °C was particularly effective, yielding the highest levels of proteins (80.0 ± 3.22 mg/g), bixin (1.60 ± 0.07 mg/g), and TPC (17.96 ± 0.90 mg GAE/g). HPLC-PDA analysis identified gallic and protocatechuic acids as dominant phenolics, with SWE extracts showing significantly higher concentrations. Additionally, SWE extracts demonstrated no cytotoxicity on Caco-2 cells up to 10.0 µg/mL. These findings highlight SWE as a prom-ising green technique for recovering proteins, natural pigments and antioxidants for food applications.
